findingMatrix.mechanism: Store actual original SDK profile parent on the matching client before invoking original launch. Scan synchronously on original SDK synchronous failure or original SDK promise rejection; register the rejection observer inside the existing wrapper before production resumes its await and disposes scratch. Return the same original promise; no filesystem-removal interception or added production API. Retain only scalar scan status/hits/phase/time. Missing/deleted/error roots are UNAVAILABLE_UNSCANNED with hits=null and required-rejection scan failure, never zero-hit proof.

Restore each capability separately and remove only after successful restoration; failed capabilities stay in their original list. Register SDK restoration groups in the outer retained list, so failed SDK/descriptor cleanup remains retryable after the client weak reference is dropped. Descriptor release rejects when any restoration attempt fails. Construction unwind still attempts every release, makes one bounded retry of remaining descriptor capabilities under the same absolute 5000ms await budget, records both construction release failures and actual descriptor/scan failures plus pending count, and computes unresolved from all of them. Original construction error is rethrown unchanged; no failure is promoted to confirmed descriptor cleanup.

instrumentationLimits: SDK rejection observer ordering and descriptor failure paths are source constructions only; no native failure was induced or executed here.

The observer registration precedes production await on the original SDK promise. No replacement SDK promise, filesystem disposal promise, raw chunks/bytes archive, secret hash or mock call records are introduced.
Missing roots in later normal cleanup may already have been disposed; they are recorded unavailable/unscanned, regardless of earlier scan result. No post-deletion absence is called a zero-hit scan.

Failed descriptor capabilities retain necessary restoration references until a retry succeeds; unresolved retained capabilities are explicitly reported. Clearing other references is not physical heap erasure.

5000ms bounds cleanup awaits, not synchronous scans or forced underlying promise/kernel settlement. Every original release remains attempted; unresolved cleanup stays failure and cannot establish native quiescence.
Historical af96 type/targetlint PASS and original extracted dataflow3 native PASS remain bound to their historical bytes. This new candidate has no current static/native PASS.
